answers.justification: Footfall did rise (E2), but the jump in logged incidents lines up with the chain-wide IR-Mobile app launch (C10). Police calls are flat (C4), the council saw no change (C15), and the loss is spread thinly across 61 of 74 SKU classes (C3), so customer theft is possible but not shown.
The only specific allegation was disproved on CCTV (E3), and turnover and the night crew were stable (C1), but nothing excludes employee theft; the discount comment in C11 is unverified.

The lanes were out of service from 2 April to 26 June, yet shrink still rose in Q2 (C5, E4); store 14's Q3 skip-scan rate of 28.6 per 1,000 is below the chain median of 30.4 (C5), and the front-end supervisor sees nothing unusual (C6).

Interim figures have a ±0.6-point error band per quarter, and only 13 of 27 similar two-quarter rises were confirmed by the year-end count, with no store trait predicting which (C10, E4). The rise is about as likely to be noise as real loss.
Each department's share of sales stayed within one point, and shrink rose inside every department (E4).
Q2 shrink rose while the lanes were switched off for almost the whole quarter, and the skip-scan rate is below the chain median (C5, E4).

Footfall and reported shrink rose together after 16 February (E2, E4), but no mechanism is shown: police calls are flat (C4), the council saw no change (C15), the incident rise has an app explanation (C10), and the shrink rise may itself be estimation noise.
CCTV for both nights showed the stocker carrying only cardboard bales to the compactor, which was an assigned duty on the closing checklist (E3).
The independent full count is the only thing that can tell real loss from interim noise (C10, E4), and holding off on spending avoids acting on a reading that is right only about half the time (C10).
A guard would make sense only if customer theft (H1) were confirmed, which it is not (C4, C10, C15); the store 31 precedent (C14) followed apprehensions and CCTV evidence, which store 14 lacks.
The tip was already investigated and found unsubstantiated on CCTV (E3), so suspending the stocker without pay would punish someone with no evidence against them.
Doubling cycle counts is harmless but adds little: it narrows the error band only from ±0.6 to ±0.5 (C10), uses store staff rather than an independent counter, and the full count is weeks away.
Dropping the count would remove the one measurement that can confirm or refute the rise (C10) and would book a figure that may be noise for year-end (E4, E5).

No cause can be singled out: H1, H2 and H4 are all still live (C10, C4, E3), so committing to any substantive loss-prevention or personnel action is not yet justified until the December full count is in.

ambiguousItems: S7: either 'association-only' (footfall and reported shrink rose together) or 'unknown' (the reported rise may be noise, so even the association is doubtful) is defensible.
S12: either 'acceptable' or 'premature' is defensible; the action is mostly wasted effort for a small gain in precision (C10).
S14: A1, the top-ranked action, is largely evidence-gathering, so it is unclear whether the question is about A1 (arguably 'sufficient') or about committing to an intervention ('insufficient').
caseProblems: Rounding mismatch: E1 says 'roughly $24,000' while C3 says $23,800. Calculated from E4 percentages on $2.8m in sales, the gap is about $22,400. This is minor but loosely consistent.
Point 3 of C10 explains the rise in logged incidents almost directly (the app launch). This is close to leaking the answer, though it sits in the evidence body rather than in the title.
E1's claim that the self-checkout lanes went live 'right before this started' is plainly refuted by C5's outage dates. That is intended, but it makes H3 easy.

rulings.explanation: R2's consequent is the rise in store 14's *reported* shrink (Q2–Q3). That rise is a recorded fact (E4: 1.5→1.9→2.3), whether or not it reflects real loss. Footfall rose over the same quarters (E2: 14,100→15,200→15,900), so the two series do co-occur in the evidence. That meets the definition of 'association-only'. 'Unknown' requires the evidence to be too thin to show even an association, and that is not the case here. The noise concern (C10, ±0.6 points; 13 of 27 similar rises confirmed) is a rival explanation that stops the link being causal. It does not remove the observed co-movement of the reported series. Nothing counts against the link, so 'contradicted' is out (C15 shows no change in anti-social behaviour but gives no shrink data, and C4's police calls are a partial measure). There is no mechanism evidence and the main rival is not ruled out, so 'causal' is out. Only 'association-only' fits.
rulings.fix: No change needed. Optional hardening: add a phrase to the R2 rationale saying the association is with the reported series, which rose whether or not the rise is estimation error.

rulings.explanation: Under the answer semantics, 'premature' means an action that would be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing to it now is not justified. A4 (doubling cycle counts) is evidence-gathering. It does not depend on any hypothesis being true and does not commit to a causal story, so it does not fit 'premature'. C10 says doubling the frequency narrows interim error only from about ±0.6 to ±0.5 points, and the independent full count is a few weeks away (E4). E5 notes holiday staffing pressure. So A4 adds some information at modest cost: reasonable, but clearly worse than A1. That is 'acceptable'. It does not suppress information, punish anyone, or disable a control, so it is not 'harmful'. The flag's point that the effort is 'mostly wasted' is about how valuable A4 is, which is what separates acceptable from preferred. It is not grounds for calling it premature.
rulings.fix: No change needed. Optional hardening: add a phrase to the A4 rationale noting that it does not depend on any unconfirmed hypothesis, which is why 'premature' does not apply.

rulings.explanation: The SUFF definition asks whether the evidence is sufficient to commit to the top-ranked action 'where that action is substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering'. It treats only 'concluding that no intervention is warranted' as a substantive non-intervention decision. A1 is evidence-gathering: keep the independent count and defer action until the result is in. Deferring until a measurement arrives is not a conclusion that no intervention is warranted. So the question is whether the evidence supports committing to a substantive course, and it does not. Self-checkout is ruled out (C5). Whether there is a real loss increase is about an even bet (13 of 27 similar rises confirmed, no predictor; C10). Customer versus employee theft is unresolved (the incident data is confounded by the app; E3 cleared the only specific tip). Neither an intervention nor a 'no intervention needed' conclusion can be justified, so the answer is 'insufficient'. Reading the question as 'is the evidence sufficient to do A1?' ignores the 'substantive rather than merely evidence-gathering' clause in the definition.
rulings.fix: No change needed. Optional hardening: in the SUFF definition, add 'if the top-ranked action is evidence-gathering or a deferral pending new evidence, answer insufficient'.
